title: Reading and setting app profile passwords through the API

prose.text: Two calls touch app profile passwords outside the full app profile edit: one reads the passwords that apply to a user on an OS, one sets passwords on a named profile rule. Paths and SDK coverage are generated.

prose.label: Reading.
prose.text: What `getPasswords` returns, and that a caller who can read it gets the passwords in plain text: [[zcc.api.devices-wire:passwords]], [[zcc.api.devices-wire:secrets-on-get]].

prose.label: Setting.
prose.text: The `managePass` body: [[zcc.api.company-wire:manage-pass-contract]]. {{manage-pass-call}} {{device-type-codes}} {{zad-zdp-names}} The Python SDK has no method that sends it: [[zcc.api.company-wire:manage-pass-python-model-only]].

prose.label: Go SDK.
prose.text: The Go `UpdateManagePass` sends an empty JSON object instead of its payload: [[shared.sdk-go.request-handling:zcc-request-do-double-marshals]].

prose.label: Two surfaces.
prose.text: The app profile object also carries per-service disable passwords, and which of the two wins when both are set is open {{gap:surface-authority}}.

checks.do: For a password change made through `managePass` from Go that had no effect, whether the request body was empty.
Whether the API key behind a `managePass` call has full App Profiles access with write permission.
Whether a password was also set on the app profile itself, before deciding which value the device enforces.

manage-pass-call.statement: `managePass` requires `policyName` and `deviceType`, and the token must belong to a user with full access to Client Connector App Profiles, with an API key created with write access.

expect.description: Updates profile policy rule passwords. The JSON Web Token (JWT) passed in as a header must be associated with a user who has Full access to Zscaler Client Connector App Profiles with an API key created with Write access. To learn more, see Adding Roles and Adding an API Key.
Supports adding and updating profile policy rule passwords.

device-type-codes.statement: The `managePass` `deviceType` codes are 1 iOS, 2 Android, 3 Windows, 4 macOS, 5 Linux and 6 Other.

expect.description:
Device type can be one of the following values:

  • 1 - iOS
  • 2 - Android
  • 3 - Windows
  • 4 - macOS
  • 5 - Linux
  • 6 - Other

zad-zdp-names.statement: The `managePass` contract describes `zadDisablePass` as the password to disable Zscaler Active Defense (ZAD) and `zdpDisablePass` as the password to disable Zscaler Deception.

expect.description: Password to disable Zscaler Active Defense (ZAD).

surface-authority.title: Which password surface wins: the app profile's own fields or `managePass`
surface-authority.detail: The Python web policy model's `policyExtension` object (class `PolicyExtension`) carries `exitPassword`, `zdxDisablePassword`, `zdDisablePassword`, `zpaDisablePassword` and `zdpDisablePassword` (and no `ziaDisablePassword`), while `managePass` sets `exitPass`, `logoutPass`, `uninstallPass` and ZIA, ZPA, ZDX, ZDP and ZAD disable passwords per rule and device type, and `getPasswords` returns a `zdSettingsAccessPass`. Which value applies when both surfaces set one, and how `zdDisablePassword`, `zdSettingsAccessPass` and `zadDisablePass` relate, is not stated.
surface-authority.blocks: predicting which password a device enforces after changes through both surfaces
